title: ADR - Telemetry Stencil for Feature-Gated Runtime Emission
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Summary:
This ADR establishes a small, enforceable contract between runtime feature gates (flags and staged rollouts) and the code that emits telemetry for them. Each gated feature ships with a 'telemetry stencil': a minimal, versioned schema describing exactly what the feature may emit. Stencils keep ingestion cost predictable, cap cardinality, and default to privacy-safe behaviour while still giving teams the observability they need during rollouts.

Problem statement and motivation:
- Several incidents over 2024 and early 2025 followed the same two patterns: experimental features driving telemetry cardinality out of control, and new gate logic that touched request structures accidentally emitting PII. Both pushed up ingestion spend and created compliance exposure.
- Teams want rollouts to stay lightweight, but they also need guardrails that stop telemetry spikes, make ownership obvious, and plug into rollout automation (canary, staged percentages, rollback).

Scope and applicability:
- Covers Redwood server-side runtimes (hosted and Dedicated) and the runtime sidecars that emit telemetry in Private deployments. Client SDKs and client-side events are out of scope here; a companion doc will apply the same principles.

Decision (contract overview):
Every new runtime gate must be accompanied by two small JSON artifacts, a Gate Manifest and a Telemetry Stencil, both registered in the feature registry and validated in CI.

1) Gate Manifest (required fields):
- gate_id (string): stable, namespaced identifier (e.g. runtimes/prio-hedging/v1).
- owner (string): team alias plus PagerDuty rotation.
- rollout_strategy (string): canary | staged | percentage.
- telemetry_stencil_id (string): the registered stencil this gate uses.
- default_state (string): enabled | disabled.
- safe_fallback (string): the fallback behaviour to revert to when SLO or telemetry limits are breached.

Validation rule: CI fails any change that adds or modifies a gate without a telemetry_stencil_id, or that references a stencil not present in the registry.

2) Telemetry Stencil (required fields):
- stencil_id (string): namespaced identifier (e.g. stencils/prio-hedging/basic-v1).
- version (string): semver-style ("1.0.0").
- field_list (list of strings): ordered field descriptors emitted while the gate is active, formatted "name|type|cardinality_hint|privacy_hint" (e.g. "prompt_hash|string|low|pii-free").
- max_estimated_egress_per_minute (string): estimated MB/min.
- privacy_profile (string): pii-free | pii-reduced | pii-allowed.
- retention_days (string): retention in days, as a numeric string.

Ingestion and alerting pipelines use the cardinality and privacy hints as guidance. In production the runtime never emits fields outside field_list; only an explicit dev/debug mode may do so.

Operational guarantees and enforcement:
- Bounded cost: every stencil declares an egress estimate, and runtime plus ingestion account emissions against it. When measured egress for a gate goes beyond 2x the declared max, the runtime starts automated mitigation (see Rollout & Runbook).
- Privacy safe-by-default: hosted deployments may use stencils with privacy_profile pii-free or pii-reduced without extra legal review. Private deployments can use pii-allowed with approval.
- Observability fidelity: stencil fields are sampled at 100% during the initial canary; once the canary passes, teams drop to a post-canary target (e.g. 25%) chosen on cost/SLO grounds.

Registration and CI workflow:
1) The developer writes the stencil JSON and gate manifest and opens a PR against the feature registry repo.
2) CI checks schema conformance, plausibility of the egress estimate against historical baselines for comparable gates/models, owner/LDAP resolution, and that hosted-approved stencils carry no PII hints.
3) On merge the registry issues a manifest fingerprint, which is embedded in deployment artifacts so the rollout is pinned to the approved stencil.

Runtime behavior specification:
- Load: stencil metadata is loaded at startup and cached by stencil_id + version.
- Emit: while a gate is active only field_list fields are emitted; anything else is dropped and the internal metric 'telemetry.emission.unexpected_fields' is incremented.
- Annotate: traces and logs carry gate_id and stencil_version for filtering.
- Accounting: per-gate egress counters are reported to the telemetry-cost pipeline at 1m granularity.

Rollout and runbook:
1) Canary: default 5% traffic, 2 cycles (default cycle = 1 hour), stencil fields sampled at 100%.
2) Monitor: per-gate egress rate, per-field cardinality, and SLOs (p50/p95 latency, error rate) on the rollout dashboard.
3) Mitigation thresholds:
   - Warning: measured_egress > 1.5 * declared_max => reduce telemetry sampling to 25% and notify the owner.
   - Critical: measured_egress > 2.0 * declared_max OR SLO regression > 5% sustained for 3 cycles => automated rollback to safe_fallback and page on-call.

Rollback pseudo-code (runtime):
if measured_egress(gate_id) > 2.0 * declared_max:
  emit_alert("telemetry-egress-critical", gate_id)
  trigger_rollout_action(gate_id, action="rollback-to-fallback")

Example stencil:
{
  "stencil_id": "stencils/prio-hedging/basic-v1",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "field_list": [
    "gate_id|string|low|pii-free",
    "request_id|string|low|pii-free",
    "heuristic_score|float|low|pii-reduced",
    "latency_ms|int|low|pii-free"
  ],
  "max_estimated_egress_per_minute": "0.75",
  "privacy_profile": "pii-reduced",
  "retention_days": "30"
}

Configuration defaults (recommended):
- rollout.canary_percent = 5
- telemetry.default_sampling = 100
- telemetry.post_canary_sampling = 25
- telemetry.egress_throttle_ratio = 2.0

Migration plan and compatibility:
- Gates that already exist without a stencil get a 3-month remediation window. In that window the platform auto-attaches a conservative system stencil (pii-reduced, max_estimated_egress_per_minute=0.1MB/min) and opens a remediation ticket.
- Private deployments may loosen privacy_profile enforcement but must still register stencils and run CI validation against their private registry.

Consequences and trade-offs:
- Pros: predictable telemetry cost for rollouts, fewer surprise ingestion spikes, clearer ownership, earlier detection of PII leakage.
- Cons: extra authoring work and some friction for fast experiments. To offset this we will provide a minimal "fast-track" stencil template and CLI scaffolding.

Open questions:
- Egress estimation for bursty, long-completion models: start with a conservative worst-case token multiplier and refine it with a historical multiplier job.
- Scoped debug sampling for individual request IDs: proposal is a gated debug channel restricted by role-based access with short TTLs.

Ownership and success metrics:
- Owner: runtime-observability team (primary contact: Priya Natarajan).
- Adoption target: every new gate registered with a stencil once the 3-month migration window closes.
- Reliability target: no severe telemetry incidents caused by new gate rollouts, year over year.

Related documentation:
- Telemetry ingestion and retention guidelines (see related_pages).
- Runtime sidecar contract for private deployments.
